South Korea Asks Qatar for Priority LNG Once Hormuz Reopens

South Korea has asked Qatar to prioritize LNG supply to the Asian nation when traffic through the Strait of Hormuz normalizes, South Korea’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said on Monday.

Qatar, the world’s second-largest LNG exporter before the Iran war, has struggled to ship LNG carriers through the Strait of Hormuz, and gas flows have recovered only slightly, especially compared to the crude flows out of the Persian Gulf and the chokepoint.

The Strait of Hormuz crisis hasn’t allowed many Qatari LNG cargoes to transit Hormuz since March. State-owned QatarEnergy has been extending the force majeure on deliveries every month since April, with the latest extension until the end of December 2026, at the very least.

Soaring prices of spot LNG supply amid the lack of Middle Eastern deliveries have pushed South Korea to rely more on coal-fired power generation in the coming winter, despite its pledge to shift away from fossil fuels.

Gas-fired power generation in South Korea and Japan crashed earlier this year as the Middle East crisis began. In South Korea, coal-fired power supply soared by 40% in April, the biggest jump since August 2019, according to market data cited by Reuters.

Like all other Asian importers, South Korea, the world’s third-largest LNG buyer after China and Japan, has been hit by the Middle East crisis and the lack of Qatari LNG supply. Soaring spot LNG prices for supply not needing the Strait of Hormuz have made running gas-fired plants uneconomical compared to coal.

“In the short term, we are in a situation where we must somehow reduce LNG demand,” Climate, Energy and Environment Minister Kim Sungwhan told Bloomberg last month.

Looking beyond the current Hormuz constraints, Kim Jung-kwan, South Korea’s Minister of Trade, Industry and Resources, on Monday met with Qatar’s Minister of State for Energy Affairs, Saad Sherida al-Kaabi, in Seoul, and asked for priority access to Qatar’s gas for Korea when Qatari LNG production and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz return to normal.
